title: Post-incident customer summary and verification checklist
content:
Summary for customers (short):

On 2026-08-02 21:12 UTC we observed a period of degraded inference responses for a subset of hosted API requests in the eu-west region. Customers experienced increased latency and, for some routed requests, truncated or out-of-order structured outputs for up to 63 minutes. Normal service resumed after staged rollbacks and targeted cache invalidation at 22:15 UTC.

What we are sharing here: a concise timeline, technical root cause in plain language, actions Redwood took to restore service, what customers can (optionally) do to verify their data and outputs, and next steps to reduce recurrence risk.

Impact scope:
- Affected customers: tenants routed through eu-west inference clusters during 21:12–22:15 UTC.
- Symptoms: elevated 95/99 latency, streaming truncations for structured outputs, and a small number of duplicate or partial tokens in multi-chunk responses.
- Data integrity: we found no evidence of data exfiltration or permanent data loss. Some responses served during the window may be incomplete; request logs and request/response snapshots are preserved for customer verification on request.

High-level root cause (plain language):
- A recent runtime change to KV-cache eviction scheduling interacted with a load spike in one autoscaling group. Under this traffic pattern the runtime occasionally attempted to serve from a partially-populated KV cache while a background eviction job simultaneously reclaimed references. This produced transient incorrect cache lookups for a narrow set of sequence-length and batching patterns, which led to truncated outputs and repeated token fragments in streaming sessions.

What we did (chronology of remediation):
- 21:14 UTC: Incident detected via synthetic latency alerts and streaming error traces.
- 21:20 UTC: Scoped impact to eu-west GPU pool and temporarily disabled the new eviction scheduling change for the affected node pool.
- 21:30 UTC: Began safe cache flush for impacted shards and placed those shards into a bypass mode so requests would be served from cold KV paths while rebuild completed.
- 21:52 UTC: Rollback flag propagated; routing began shifting traffic to standby healthy pools.
- 22:15 UTC: Latency and truncation rates returned to baseline.
- 22:30 UTC: Post-recovery verification completed on sampling of tenant traces; began preservation of full evidence package for customers who request it.

Customer verification checklist (recommended, optional):
1) Confirm if you observed anomalous responses: check your application logs for requests between 2026-08-02 21:12–22:15 UTC and note any truncated/partial outputs.
2) Sanity-check outputs: run a small sample of previously-cached prompts against the same model/version and compare token counts and structure.
3) If you use streaming, validate that message boundaries match expectations for the same prompts.
4) For customers concerned about replay integrity: request the preserved request/response snapshots from Redwood (see contact below). We will provide a signed evidence package with request timestamp, routed node id, and service-side transcript.
5) Optional token rotation: if your security policy requires, rotate API keys used during the incident window. No compromise detected, but rotation is offered for peace of mind.

What customers can expect from Redwood right now:
- We will proactively reach out to tenants we know were routed to the impacted pool with tailored evidence packages and a short reconciliation guide.
- Customers can request a custom evidence export (signed) for their tenant id; we aim to deliver this within 48 business hours of request.
- A follow-up note will be posted to the public status page and to customers who subscribe to eu-west incident updates.

Technical mitigation and longer-term changes (what we are doing to prevent recurrence):
- Reverting the eviction scheduling change in all active pools until a hardening release is validated under wider load shapes.
- Adding an invariant check in the runtime that detects partially-populated KV cache reads and triggers a safe fallback to cold paths rather than returning partial data.
- Expanding our synthetic tests to include sequence-length and batching combinations that previously escaped coverage.
- Enhancing routing policy so a single autoscaling group's transient failure cannot expose multiple tenant routing lanes concurrently.

Customer-facing timeline (to be used as status page content):
- 2026-08-02 21:12 UTC — First alerts: elevated latency and streaming truncations in eu-west.
- 2026-08-02 21:20 UTC — Scoped to a single GPU node pool; mitigation actions started.
- 2026-08-02 21:52 UTC — Rollback initiated and traffic rebalanced.
- 2026-08-02 22:15 UTC — Service metrics returned to normal; monitoring continued.
- 2026-08-03 — Draft customer post-incident note prepared and evidence collection started.

How to request evidence or support (owner / SLA):
- Primary contact: customer-success-ops@redwood.ai (attn: Asha Kapoor).
- For enterprise customers with a designated TAM, open a priority ticket referencing JIRA-OPS-1342; we will attach a signed evidence package.
- If you need expedited delivery (within 24 hours), include your tenant id and the phrase "URGENT EVIDENCE" in the ticket subject.

Short FAQ (anticipated customer questions):
Q: Was my data accessed or modified?
A: No indication of exfiltration or external access. The issue affected output assembly inside the serving runtime; stored customer data was not modified.

Q: Can you guarantee results were incorrect for all requests during the window?
A: No. Many requests were served correctly; only a subset that matched the cache-eviction + sequence-length pattern were impacted. We will provide per-request evidence on request.

Q: Do I need to replay user requests to fix my application state?
A: Only if you detect application-visible errors or truncated results that affected downstream state. For most read-only generator calls, reissuing the request will produce a correct response once the mitigations are in place.

Draft status notes / internal pointers (for CS leads):
- This doc is intentionally compact for customer distribution; a longer internal technical postmortem with traces and flame graphs is being prepared by serving-runtime and applied-ml.
- Linked internal work: JIRA-OPS-1342 (eviction scheduling rollback), PR#6732 (runtime invariant checks), CONFLUENCE-INC-4821 (internal evidence bundle).

Suggested next external touchpoints:
- Within 48 hours: personalized evidence package emailed to impacted tenants on request.
- Within 7 days: a technical postmortem summarized for enterprise customers with additional risk-reduction timelines.
- Within 30 days: follow-up update describing verification of the hardening release and synthetic coverage expansion.

Appendix: Example verification steps we will perform for a tenant on request:
- Provide per-request transcript with node id, token deltas, and evidence of fallback behavior.
- Run a deterministic replay of selected requests against a patched runtime to produce a side-by-side diff.
- Provide a signed manifest (SHA256) of evidence files and a short integrity report.

End of draft.

Notes to self: convert this to a statuspage-friendly short blurb (<= 300 chars) + a longer customer email template. Coordinate with SRE for final evidence export SLA before sending to customers.
